proposals: The Ministry of Mines should publish an annual estimate of end-of-life copper and aluminium generated in India and the share collected by authorised recyclers, so the reverse-logistics gap behind $8 billion a year of imported scrap is measured rather than inferred from trade data.

The Ministry of Mines should report quarterly disbursements under the ₹1,500 crore National Critical Mineral Mission recycling incentive with tonnes of copper and aluminium recovered from domestic waste, so the scheme can be judged against the imported-scrap line it is meant to replace.

The Department of Revenue should publish, six months after any change to precious-metal customs duties, a review of imports across adjacent HS lines and source countries, so migrations like platinum alloy collapsing 92 per cent while bare gold and doré rose are tracked officially.

The Central Pollution Control Board should publish quarterly volumes and prices of EPR certificates traded for end-of-life solar modules, so it can be seen whether certificate trading is closing the ₹10,000–12,000 a tonne loss on PV recycling before high-silver modules enter the waste stream.
